current.text: He is a backup center behind Nick Claxton, whom Chicago acquired in June. The September team preview listed him third off the bench, after Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro, with Buddy Hield behind him.

Experts disagree on his opening-night role. The September 28 preview put Claxton at about 90% to start and did not expect Smith to start. A mock draft on October 14 guessed Smith will start at center on opening night.
He has a foot issue now.
If he starts, he is a must-roster player because of his shooting and blocks.
He is a late flyer or swing pick. Experts call him an easy draft in 16-team leagues and debatable in 14-team leagues. One expert took him around pick 157 as an early-season flyer.
Do not trust his numbers from March and April of last season.
Chicago could make him expendable and trade him if Leonard Miller develops. A later note says Miller is stuck behind Buzelis and Caleb Wilson.
Chicago has 10 games in our fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21 (3-3-4).

durable.text: In his career he has tended to get hurt just as more playing time opens up.
His fantasy appeal is threes and blocks from a big man. His points, assists and steals are low.

note: Both sites give him a 0 USD value. He ranks 157 at Yahoo and 201 at ESPN, outside the 144 players our 12-team auction takes, and experts call him debatable even in 14-team leagues. So do not spend on him at the draft. Watch who starts at center on opening night and how his foot recovers. If he starts or Claxton misses time, his threes and blocks (1.4 3PM and 0.8 BLK projected in about 20 minutes) make him a quick FAB add.
